_comment_simulator_version: simulator-v2: heterogeneous zones. NOT comparable to simulator-v1 results.
_comment_global_scalars: Global scalars kept for backward-compatibility with v1 tests. Simulator-v2 uses per-zone arrays below.
_comment_per_zone: SYNTHETIC ASSUMPTIONS — frozen before any training. Values chosen to create physically meaningful zone heterogeneity, not to make RL win.

_zone_layout.Zone-A: Edge zone, moderate heat gain, moderate cooling effectiveness, good COP.
_zone_layout.Zone-B: Core zone, lower heat gain (dense but efficient servers), high cooling effectiveness (dedicated CRAC unit), best COP. Preferred migration destination.
_zone_layout.Zone-D: Impaired zone: older server generation (higher heat gain), partially obstructed airflow (lower cooling effectiveness), aging cooling unit (worst COP). Primary migration source.
_zone_layout.Zone-E: Warm-aisle zone, elevated heat gain due to recirculation, below-average cooling effectiveness and COP.

_zone_heat_gain_note: SYNTHETIC ASSUMPTION. a_i: degrees-C rise per unit workload per step. Zone-D is highest (older servers, more heat per compute unit). Zone-B is lowest (efficient hardware).
_zone_cooling_effectiveness_note: SYNTHETIC ASSUMPTION. b_i: degrees-C cooling removal per unit cooling command per step. Zone-B has dedicated CRAC (high b). Zone-D has partially obstructed airflow (low b). Range: 4.0 to 8.0.
_zone_cop_note: SYNTHETIC ASSUMPTION. COP_i: coefficient of performance — thermal kW removed per electrical kW consumed. Zone-B has newest cooling unit (COP=3.8). Zone-D has aging unit (COP=2.0). Lower COP = more electrical power per unit of cooling.
_zone_ambient_coupling_note: SYNTHETIC ASSUMPTION. g_i: per-zone ambient coupling. Kept uniform at v1 default; can be differentiated in future work.
_zone_adjacency_note: SYNTHETIC ASSUMPTION. adjacency[i][j] = fraction of zone i heat that recirculates into zone j. Set to all-zeros in v2 (no inter-zone recirculation). Non-zero values may be added in future work.
_comment_v2_migration_effect: Moving 0.2 workload from Zone-D to Zone-B: (1) reduces heat generated (a_D=5.8 -> a_B=4.5, saving 0.2*1.3=0.26 deg/step of heat); (2) more effective cooling in Zone-B (b_B=8.0 vs b_D=4.0, needs less cooling action to maintain same temperature); (3) less electrical power per unit cooling in Zone-B (COP_B=3.8 vs COP_D=2.0). Net effect: measurable reduction in total electrical cooling power.
_it_power_note: IT power is determined by server hardware, not cooling unit. Kept uniform. Cooling electrical power is separately modelled via COP.
_cooling_power_max_note: SYNTHETIC ASSUMPTION. Maximum thermal power removal capacity per zone cooling unit (kW). Electrical power consumed = thermal_removal_kw / COP_i.
_legacy_comment: a=heat-from-workload, b=cooling-removal, g=ambient-coupling. In v2, these are per-zone (zone_heat_gain_coefficients, zone_cooling_effectiveness, zone_ambient_coupling). Global scalars above are v1 backward-compatibility only.
